0: Across all four datasets, increase the existing causal recent-four-state pooling contribution from 0.2 to 0.35: use 0.65*h_t + 0.35*mean(last four nonpadding states ending at t). The previous pooling gain motivates testing stronger recent-context smoothing. Apply at every training position and the final real inference position; synchronize predictor metadata. Keep truncation, embeddings, backbone, scoring, loss and optimizer fixed.
1: Across all four datasets, change the six causal convolution blocks' dilation schedule from [1,2,4,8,1,2] to [1,2,4,1,2,4], retaining both convolutions per block. Most histories are short, so emphasizing nearby interactions may reduce sparse long-range mixing while retaining sufficient receptive field. Preserve features, embeddings, readout, scoring, loss and optimizer; synchronize the predictor architecture.
2: Across all four datasets, construct the existing input frequency feature as sqrt(log1p(training_count)/max_log_count), keeping the attenuation formula 1-0.3*feature unchanged. This increases attenuation for moderately frequent historical items while leaving unseen items unattenuated, potentially improving specificity beyond suppressing only the most frequent items. Use training interactions only; preserve embedding design, topology, readout, loss and optimizer, and save the feature buffer in each category checkpoint.
3: Across all four datasets, retain pointwise positive-plus-negative logistic loss but average valid positions within each sampled sequence first, then average sequences, instead of averaging globally over positions. Equal sequence weighting may prevent longer histories from dominating updates and better match user-averaged HR@10. Preserve sampling, features, embeddings, architecture, scoring/readout, optimizer, scheduler and batch/epoch settings.
